verses.text: So Festus, as e don enter di province, after three days go up to Jerusalem from Caesarea.
Den di high priest and di principal men of di Jews inform am against Paul, and dem beg am,
dey ask favor against am, say make e summon am to Jerusalem, as dem dey plan to kill am for di way.
But Festus answer say make dem keep Paul for custody for Caesarea, and say e imself dey about to leave soon.
“So make di ones wey get power among una,” e talk, “go down with me, and if anything wrong dey for di man, make dem accuse am.”
When e don stay among dem pass ten days, e go down to Caesarea. Di next day e sit for di judgment seat, command say make dem bring Paul.
When e come, di Jews wey come down from Jerusalem stand round am, dey bring against am many and grievous charges wey dem no fit prove,
while e talk for im defense, “I no commit any offense, no against di law of di Jews, or against di temple, or against Caesar.”
But Festus, as e want gain favor with di Jews, answer Paul talk say, “You willing to go up to Jerusalem, and dem judge you there by me about these things?”
But Paul talk say, “I dey stand before Caesar judgment seat, wia dem suppose try me. I no do di Jews any wrong, as you know well well too.

Because if I be wrongdoer, and I don commit anything wey deserve death, I no refuse to die; but if none of those things wey dem accuse me of na true, nobody fit give me up to dem. I appeal to Caesar!”
Den Festus, when e don confer with di council, answer, “You don appeal to Caesar. To Caesar you go go.”
Now when some days don pass, King Agrippa and Bernice reach Caesarea and greet Festus.
As dem stay there many days, Festus lay Paul case before di king, dey talk say, “One man dey wey Felix leave as prisoner;
about whom, when I dey Jerusalem, di chief priests and di elders of di Jews inform me, dey ask for sentence against am.

I answer dem say e no be di custom of di Romans to give up any man to destruction before di accused don meet di accusers face to face, and don get chance to make im defense about di matter wey dem lay against am.
So when dem come together here, I no delay, but di next day I sit for di judgment seat, command say make dem bring di man.
About whom, when di accusers stand up, dem no bring any charge of such things as I think;
but dem get some questions against am about dem own religion, and about one Jesus, wey die, wey Paul affirm say e dey alive.
As I confuse how to inquire about these things, I ask whether e willing to go Jerusalem and dem judge am there about these matters.
But when Paul don appeal say make dem keep am for di decision of di emperor, I command say make dem keep am until I fit send am to Caesar.”
Agrippa talk to Festus say, “I want hear di man myself too.” “Tomorrow,” e talk, “you go hear am.”
So di next day, when Agrippa and Bernice come with great pomp, and dem enter di place of hearing with di commanding officers and di principal men of di city, by Festus command, dem bring Paul in.
Festus talk say, “King Agrippa, and all men wey dey here with us, una see this man wey all di crowd of di Jews petition me about, both for Jerusalem and here, dey shout say e no suppose live again.
But I find say e no commit anything wey deserve death. As e imself appeal to di emperor, I decide to send am.
About am I no get any certain thing to write to my oga. So I don bring am out before una, and especially before you, King Agrippa, so that, after examination, I go get something to write.
Because e seem to me unreasonable, as I dey send prisoner, no to specify di charges against am too.”
Agrippa talk to Paul say, “You fit talk for yourself.” Den Paul stretch out im hand, make im defense.
“I think myself happy, King Agrippa, say I go make my defense before you today about all di things wey di Jews accuse me of,
especially because you be expert for all customs and questions among di Jews. So I beg you to hear me patiently.
Truly, all di Jews know my way of life from my youth, wey be from di beginning among my own nation and for Jerusalem;
as dem don know me from di first, if dem willing to testify, say after di strictest sect of our religion, I live as Pharisee.
Now I dey stand here make dem judge me for di hope of di promise wey God make to our papa dem,
wey our 12 tribes, as dem dey serve night and day with earnestness, hope to reach. About this hope di Jews dey accuse me, King Agrippa!
Why dem judge am say e no fit believe among una, if God dey raise di dead?
I myself think for sure say I suppose do many things against di name of Jesus of Nazareth.
I do this for Jerusalem too. I lock up many of di saints inside prisons, as I don receive authority from di chief priests, and when dem kill dem I cast my vote against dem.
As I dey punish dem often for all di synagogues, I try force dem to blaspheme. As I vex well well against dem, I persecute dem even to foreign cities.
For this as I dey travel to Damascus with di authority and commission from di chief priests,
for midday, O king, I see for di way light from di sky, brighter pass di sun, dey shine round me and di people wey dey travel with me.
When we all fall to di earth, I hear voice dey talk to me, dey talk for di Hebrew language, ‘Saul, Saul, why you dey persecute me? E hard for you to kick against di goads.’
I talk say, ‘Who you be, Lord?’ E talk say, ‘I be Jesus wey you dey persecute.
But get up, stand for your feet, because I don appear to you for this purpose, to appoint you servant and witness both of di things wey you don see, and of di things wey I go reveal to you;
as I dey deliver you from di people, and from di Gentiles, wey I dey send you to,

to open dem eyes, so that dem go turn from darkness to light and from di power of Satan to God, so that dem go receive forgiveness of sins and inheritance among di people wey dem make holy by faith for me.’
So, King Agrippa, I no disobey di heavenly vision,
but I declare first to dem for Damascus, for Jerusalem, and through all di country of Judea, and to di Gentiles too, say make dem repent and turn to God, dey do works wey fit show repentance.
For this reason Jews catch me for di temple, and try kill me.
So as I don get di help wey come from God, I dey stand reach today dey testify both to small and great, dey talk nothing except wetin di prophets and Moses talk say go happen,
how di Christ must suffer, and how, by di resurrection of di dead, e go be di first to proclaim light both to these people and to di Gentiles.”
As e dey make im defense so, Festus talk with loud voice, “Paul, you don craze! Your great learning dey drive you mad!”
But e talk say, “I no craze, most excellent Festus, but I dey boldly declare words of truth and reason.
Because di king know about these things, wey I dey talk to freely too. Because I believe say none of these things hide from am, because dem no do this for corner.
King Agrippa, you believe di prophets? I know say you believe.”
Agrippa talk to Paul say, “With small persuasion you dey try make me Christian?”
Paul talk say, “I wish to God say, whether with small or with plenty, no be only you, but also all wey hear me today, go become like me, except for these bonds.”
Di king get up with di governor, and Bernice, and di people wey sit with dem.
When dem don withdraw, dem talk to each other say, “This man no do anything wey deserve death or bonds.”
Agrippa talk to Festus say, “Dem go don free this man if e no appeal to Caesar.”
When dem decide say we go sail go Italy, dem deliver Paul and some other prisoners to one centurion wey im name na Julius, of di Augustan Regiment.
As we enter ship of Adramyttium, wey dey about to sail to places for di coast of Asia, we put to sea, Aristarchus, Macedonian of Thessalonica, dey with us.
Di next day, we land for Sidon. Julius treat Paul kindly, give am permission to go meet im friends and refresh imself.
As we put to sea from there, we sail under di shelter of Cyprus, because di winds dey against us.
When we don sail cross di sea wey dey off Cilicia and Pamphylia, we reach Myra, city of Lycia.
For there di centurion find ship of Alexandria wey dey sail go Italy, and e put us on board.
When we don sail slowly many days, and reach opposite Cnidus with difficulty, as di wind no allow us go further, we sail under di shelter of Crete, opposite Salmone.
As we sail along am with difficulty, we reach one place wey dem call Fair Havens, near di city of Lasea.
When plenty time don pass and di voyage don dangerous, because di Fast don already pass, Paul warn dem,
and talk to dem say, “Oga dem, I see say di voyage go get injury and plenty loss, no be only of di cargo and di ship, but of our lives too.”
But di centurion pay more attention to di master and to di owner of di ship than to di things wey Paul talk.

Because di haven no good to spend winter for, di majority advise say make dem go to sea from there, if by any means dem fit reach Phoenix, and spend winter there, wey be port of Crete, wey dey face northeast and southeast.
When di south wind blow softly, as dem think say dem don get wetin dem want, dem lift anchor and sail along Crete, close to di shore.
But soon after, tempestuous wind wey dem call Euroclydon beat down from di shore.
When di ship catch, and no fit face di wind, we give way to am, and dem drive us along.
As we dey run under di shelter of one small island wey dem call Clauda, we fit, with difficulty, secure di boat.
After dem don lift am up, dem use cables to help reinforce di ship. As dem fear say dem go run aground for di Syrtis sand bars, dem lower di sea anchor, and so dem drive us along.
We labor well well with di storm, and di next day dem begin throw things overboard.
For di third day, dem throw out di ship equipment with dem own hands.
When neither sun nor stars shine on us for many days, and no small storm dey on us, all hope say we go survive don go.
When dem don stay long without food, Paul stand up for middle of dem, talk say, “Oga dem, una suppose listen to me, and no sail from Crete, and get this injury and loss.
Now I urge una to take courage, because no life go lose among una, but na only di ship.
Because one angel of di God wey I belong to and wey I serve stand near me this night,
dey talk say, ‘No fear, Paul. You must stand before Caesar. Look, God don grant you all di people wey dey sail with you.’
So, oga dem, take courage! Because I believe God, say e go be just as dem talk am to me.
But we must run aground for one island.”
But when di fourteenth night reach, as dem dey drive us back and forth for di Adriatic Sea, about midnight di sailors sense say dem dey near some land.
Dem take soundings, find 20 fathoms. After small time, dem take soundings again, find 15 fathoms.
As dem fear say we go run aground for rocky ground, dem throw four anchors from di back of di ship, and dey wish for daylight.
As di sailors dey try run from di ship, and don lower di boat into di sea, dey pretend say dem go lay out anchors from di front,
Paul talk to di centurion and to di soldiers, “Unless these ones stay for di ship, una no fit survive.”
Den di soldiers cut di ropes of di boat, let am fall off.
While day dey come, Paul beg dem all to take some food, dey talk say, “Today na di fourteenth day wey una dey wait and dey continue to fast, without taking anything.
So I beg una to take some food, because this na for una safety; because no hair go perish from any of una heads.”
When e don talk this, and don take bread, e thank God before all, break am, begin chop.
Den dem all encourage, and dem take food too.
For all, we be 276 souls for di ship.
When dem don chop enough, dem make di ship light, dey throw out di wheat inside di sea.
When day break, dem no recognize di land, but dem notice one bay with beach, and dem decide to run di ship onto am, if dem fit.
As dem cast off di anchors, dem leave dem for di sea, as dem dey untie di rudder ropes at di same time. As dem lift up di foresail to di wind, dem go towards di beach.
But as dem fall for place wia two seas meet, dem run di vessel aground. Di front stick and remain immovable, but di back begin break up by di violence of di waves.
Di soldiers plan na to kill di prisoners, so that none of dem go swim out and escape.
But di centurion, as e want save Paul, stop dem from dem purpose, command say make di people wey fit swim throw demself overboard first go towards di land;
and di rest, some on planks, and some on other things from di ship. So e happen say dem all escape safely reach land.
When we don escape, den we learn say di island name na Malta.
Di natives show us uncommon kindness; because dem light fire, receive us all, because of di rain wey dey, and because of di cold.
But when Paul gather bundle of sticks put am for di fire, viper come out because of di heat, hold im hand.
When di natives see di creature dey hang from im hand, dem talk to each other say, “Without doubt this man na murderer, wey, though e escape from di sea, yet Justice no allow am to live.”
But e shake off di creature enter di fire, and no harm am.
But dem expect say e go swell or fall down dead suddenly, but when dem watch for long time and see say nothing bad happen to am, dem change dem mind, talk say e be god.
Now near that place lands dey wey belong to di chief man of di island, wey im name na Publius, wey receive us and host us kindly for three days.
E happen say Publius papa dey sick with fever and dysentery. Paul enter go meet am, pray, put hands on am, heal am.
So di rest wey get diseases for di island come too and dem heal.
Dem honor us with many honors too; and when we sail, dem put on board di things wey we need.
After three months we sail for ship of Alexandria wey don spend winter for di island, wey im figurehead na “Di Twin Brothers.”
As we touch Syracuse, we stay there three days.
From there we go round come reach Rhegium. After one day, south wind rise, and for di second day we come Puteoli,
wia we find brothers, and dem beg us to stay with dem for seven days. So we come Rome.
From there di brothers, when dem hear about our coming, come meet us reach di Market of Appius and di Three Taverns. When Paul see dem, e thank God, take courage.
When we enter Rome, di centurion deliver di prisoners to di captain of di guard, but dem allow Paul to stay by imself with di soldier wey dey guard am.

After three days Paul call together di leaders of di Jews. When dem come together, e talk to dem say, “I, brothers, though I no do anything against di people, or di customs of our papa dem, still dem deliver me as prisoner from Jerusalem into di hands of di Romans,
wey, when dem examine me, want free me, because no reason for death dey inside me.
But when di Jews talk against am, dem force me to appeal to Caesar, no be say I get anything to accuse my nation of.
For this reason I ask to see una and talk with una. Because of di hope of Israel na with this chain dem tie me.”
Dem talk to am say, “We no receive letters from Judea about you, and none of di brothers come here report or talk any evil about you.
But we want hear from you wetin you think. Because about this sect, we know say everywhere dem dey talk against am.”

When dem don appoint am one day, many people come to am for im lodging. E explain to dem, dey testify about God Kingdom, and dey persuade dem about Jesus, both from di law of Moses and from di prophets, from morning reach evening.
Some believe di things wey dem talk, and some no believe.
When dem no agree among demself, dem leave after Paul don talk one word, “Holy Spirit talk well through Isaiah di prophet to una papa dem,
dey talk say, ‘Go to this people, talk say, as una dey hear una go hear, but una no go understand at all; as una dey see una go see, but una no go perceive at all:

because this people heart don hard, dem ears no dey hear well, and dem don close dem eyes; if e no be so, perhaps dem go see with dem eyes, hear with dem ears, understand with dem heart, and turn again, and I go heal dem.’
So make una know say dem don send this salvation of God to di Gentiles. Dem go listen too.”
When e don talk these words, di Jews leave, as dem get great dispute among demself.
Paul live two whole years for im own rented house, receive all wey come meet am,
dey preach God Kingdom and dey teach di things about Lord Jesus Christ with all boldness, without hindrance.
